Senses.Explanation: The recurring line says that what falls with a thud is no other thing; some cases stage it by dropping a staff or whisk, while Gulin preserves it metrically. Gulin preserves the recurring line in verse, Zhenjing drops the staff and asks what the thing is, Xiaoshan repeats the pair after throwing down the whisk, and Feiyin does so with the staff.

Senses.PreferredTarget: When it falls, it is no other thing; moving freely, it is not dust.
SearchAliases: When it falls, it is no other thing
Senses.Note: An ordinary object or act is shown without being made into a separate defiling thing. The first clause can refer to a dropped object in the source turn; it is not an abstract metaphysical proof.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X70/X70n1378.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Wuming Huixing. In a short hall address at Beishan Zhidu monastery, Wuming Huixing describes refreshing air entering his sleeves, a clear breeze reaching every side, and white clouds embracing a secluded rock whose chill reserve becomes still more unusual. He ends with the eight-sided openness and the sheer face no one dares peer into. There is no monk's question, staff action or recorded reply inside this unit. The pair turns the landscape's freely circulating air and withdrawn rock into a pointed contrast, without naming an object that can be captured as its final meaning. Nearby poems about spring and later monastery sections are separate addresses. The source title names Wuming Huixing; a similarly styled roster master with a different personal name is not substituted for him.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X70/X70n1389.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Xisou Shaotan. At winter solstice, Xisou Shaotan pictures gathering the great world on a fingernail and kicking an ancient Buddha from a foot, then says Linji's descendants do not submit to reflective inspection. He gives the pair and follows with pearls rolling on a tray without leaving a trace: why calculate the season by declining darkness and growing light? Everyday clothes and fruit are handled freely, and paths and verbal entanglements cut away. Yet he checks the expansive ease with the need for bone-piercing cold before plum fragrance. A separately raised case then has Baizhang demand speech without throat or lips, only to be answered by three teachers' counterquestions. The couplet is Xisou's current turn, not a quoted answer by one of those later figures; its openness is joined to exacting examination rather than a blanket promise that any spontaneous act suffices.

Thanking the monastery's two groups of officers, Pingshi Rudi describes old and new sustaining one another, advance and retreat fitting the occasion, and distinct positions working responsively. They open people's eyes, extend the ancestral household and meet each situation with a way out. Even speaking like this, he says, remains within the present age. What sentence does not fall within it? He gives the eight-sided and sheer-sided pair. The immediate issue is the adequacy of his own account of successful institutional and teaching activity, not a complaint that the officers failed. ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 笑倒嵩山破竈墮。上堂。上下三指，彼此七馬。眼見如盲，口說如啞。拄杖子，忍俊不禁，等閑捉敗。休休，盡法恐無民，旦放天寒赦。達磨祖師忌拈香，不紹金輪尊貴位。被人打落當門齒，難嚲梁王掘地埋。脫身留得空棺履，死款供成，臨文不諱。乳竇今朝報不平，臭烟蓬㶿薰他鼻。任是老頑，也須噴啑。上堂。從上若佛若祖，峻機雄辯，狹路通衢，列派分宗，圖王覇業。殊不知三傳作而春秋廢，九師興而易道亡。乳峰這裏憨憨癡癡，百醜千拙，飢來喫飯，困來打眠，不知寒暑之往來，不知生死之交謝，但見皇風成一片，不知何處是封疆。上堂，舉二僧見風吹剎旛，一僧云：風動。一僧云：旛動。爭論未已，六祖見廼云：非風旛動，仁者心動。這擔柴漢，黃梅席上竊得衣盂，半夜三更驚忙奔走，及見風旛便言心動，也是作賊人心虗。雖然，只如風旛未動，何處求心？還知麼？烟雨溟濛望眼迷，蘭舟小泊畫橋西，兒童不識春流漲，却恠湖邊柳樹低。冬節，小參。捏聚大千指甲上，塵塵法界；踢出古佛脚尖頭，步步寒花。臨濟兒孫不受鑑覺，玲瓏八面自回合，峭峻一方誰敢窺？盤珠板丸了無留影，說甚陰極陽生、道消道長？赫赤布裩隨時換替，豈容皓老書佛名？團欒果子信手撮拏，未許洞山知滋味。剗除玄路，截斷葛藤，飯餘散步出松關，遠看青山近飛瀑。雖然，不是一番寒徹骨，爭得梅花撲鼻香？復舉百丈問溈山云：併却咽喉唇吻，道將一句來。溈山云：却請和尚道。丈又問道吾，吾云：和尚也須併却。丈又問雲巖，巖云：和尚有也未？丁公七箭鎻喉法，善用者不露鋒鋩。百丈老人雖解發箭，不能中的，返被羣驍攢箭射殺。雖然如是，李將軍有嘉聲在，不得封侯也是閑。上堂。天寒人寒，滴水滴凍，赤脚走冰稜，力負千鈞重，堪笑霜趺擁葉人。漆桶漆桶。永明壽禪師忌拈香。埜客吟殘，中巖月落，坐斷白雲，死不再活，只將宗鏡鑑惟心，法眼重重添翳膜。翳無藥，光爍爍，要識永明妙旨。更添香著。上堂。發得一機活，出得一言當，萬里無片雲，青天合喫棒，不待春風著意吹，暗香已在梅花上。上堂。舉馬大師同百丈游山次，見野鴨子飛過，師云：是什麼？丈云：野鴨子。師云：什麼處去也？丈云：飛過去。師遂扭丈鼻頭，丈忍痛失聲，師云：你道飛過去，因什麼在這裏？丈悟去後，歸在寮中，或時笑、或時哭云云。川僧素無頭腦，步步引人入草，忽驚野鴨群飛，便把鼻頭捏扭，哭不成哭、笑不成笑，只因家富小兒嬌，七世門風

At winter solstice, Xisou Shaotan pictures gathering the great world on a fingernail and kicking an ancient Buddha from a foot, then says Linji's descendants do not submit to reflective inspection. He gives the pair and follows with pearls rolling on a tray without leaving a trace: why calculate the season by declining darkness and growing light? Everyday clothes and fruit are handled freely, and paths and verbal entanglements cut away. Yet he checks the expansive ease with the need for bone-piercing cold before plum fragrance. A separately raised case then has Baizhang demand speech without throat or lips, only to be answered by three teachers' counterquestions. The couplet is Xisou's current turn, not a quoted answer by one of those later figures; its openness is joined to exacting examination rather than a blanket promise that any spontaneous act suffices.

Senses.Explanation: Open on all eight sides, freely meeting and turning together, yet steep in one direction where no one dares peer: the pair puts unobstructed responsiveness beside an inaccessible edge. Each local use tests that conjunction; neither pleasant harmony alone nor an isolated, unapproachable position explains the whole pair. In a short hall address at Beishan Zhidu monastery, Wuming Huixing describes refreshing air entering his sleeves, a clear breeze reaching every side, and white clouds embracing a secluded rock whose chill reserve becomes still more unusual. He ends with the eight-sided openness and the sheer face no one dares peer into. There is no monk's question, staff action or recorded reply inside this unit. The pair turns the landscape's freely circulating air and withdrawn rock into a pointed contrast, without naming an object that can be captured as its final meaning. Nearby poems about spring and later monastery sections are separate addresses. The source title names Wuming Huixing; a similarly styled roster master with a different personal name is not substituted for him. At winter solstice, Xisou Shaotan pictures gathering the great world on a fingernail and kicking an ancient Buddha from a foot, then says Linji's descendants do not submit to reflective inspection. He gives the pair and follows with pearls rolling on a tray without leaving a trace: why calculate the season by declining darkness and growing light? Everyday clothes and fruit are handled freely, and paths and verbal entanglements cut away. Yet he checks the expansive ease with the need for bone-piercing cold before plum fragrance. A separately raised case then has Baizhang demand speech without throat or lips, only to be answered by three teachers' counterquestions. The couplet is Xisou's current turn, not a quoted answer by one of those later figures; its openness is joined to exacting examination rather than a blanket promise that any spontaneous act suffices. Thanking the monastery's two groups of officers, Pingshi Rudi describes old and new sustaining one another, advance and retreat fitting the occasion, and distinct positions working responsively. They open people's eyes, extend the ancestral household and meet each situation with a way out. Even speaking like this, he says, remains within the present age. What sentence does not fall within it? He gives the eight-sided and sheer-sided pair. The immediate issue is the adequacy of his own account of successful institutional and teaching activity, not a complaint that the officers failed. Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X69/X69n1350.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baoning Renyong. Sitting upright on a cushion and passing thread through a needle's eye form a plain, precise pair of actions. Baoning Renyong's verse follows Mazu's reply when asked about his illness: 'Sun-face Buddha, moon-face Buddha.' After the sitting and threading lines, a gust of west wind brings down two or three leaves. The verse offers ordinary posture, work and seasonal movement in response to the illness case, without supplying a medical account or assigning one action to each named Buddha.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1420.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chushi Fanqi.
